source.title: Belfast Telegraph, 5 June 1964, p. 4 ("Antrim: county council election results")
source.publisher: Belfast Telegraph (via the British Newspaper Archive)
source.check: 24 divisions, 25 seats (Newtownabbey two). Unopposed names and divisions from the returning officer's notice of result (Belfast Newsletter, 6 June 1964, p. 10); votes for the three contested divisions from the Belfast Telegraph, 5 June 1964, p. 4.

note: Triennial election of Antrim County Council. The official notice (Irish News, 7 May 1964, p. 2) fixed the day of election as Thursday 4 June 1964; nomination day was Tuesday 19 May and withdrawals closed at 5 p.m. on Wednesday 20 May. Three divisions went to a poll on 4 June: Ballymoney, Carrickfergus and Newtownabbey. The returning officer's 'County of Antrim: notice of result of elections, 1964' (Belfast Newsletter, 6 June 1964, p. 10) names the member elected for every division, including the twenty-one returned unopposed; it also prints Finaghy, which the earlier nomination notice had omitted. Printed: 'Ballymoney - Henry McC. Carton, 940. Not elected - Archibald Stewart, 588. Electorate 4,715. Total votes cast 1,534. Spoiled votes five.' The printed total poll is one more than the two votes plus the five spoiled papers; it is recorded in this note rather than as a total_poll the votes do not support.
